challenge.description: Deliver at least 10 MW average grid electricity at year 10, using the least mined Mercury ore. Fixed seed, imported-tech reserve, efficiencies and transmission hardware.

warnings: Illustrative engineering scenario; no forecast of construction cost or readiness.
Circular display orbits are schematic. Collisions, eccentricity, station keeping and launch trajectories are not integrated.
Seed plant, imported technology reserve and Earth relay infrastructure are starting endowments; their delivery and capital cost are excluded.
Imported precision components are exhausted; industrial self-replication is not assumed.
Ground beam intensity or instantaneous grid capacity curtails transmission.

proposal.title: Seed-powered production with no factory expansion
proposal.rationale: Use the existing seed plant for industry, retain no manufactured mass for factory expansion, and allocate all orbital electricity to delivery. The inner orbit increases generation per collector; the radiator ratio is just above the stated thermal cutoff requirement. The baseline reports transmission curtailment, suggesting substantially fewer collectors may still meet the target. Eliminating reinvestment and expansion should reduce mining while avoiding production that adds no useful grid delivery. The host engine must verify whether seed-only production reaches the target within ten years; link saturation and the narrow thermal margin remain uncertainties.

proposal.title: Test lower mining at the outer orbit
proposal.rationale: Keep reinvestment and factory expansion at zero. Test whether the longer transfer from Mercury to 1 AU increases energy spent per launched kilogram, reducing mining under the fixed seed-power budget. Use the minimum radiator ratio to maximize collector area per manufactured kilogram while satisfying the stated thermal constraint. The previous proposal reached transmission curtailment, suggesting room to trade excess generation for lower mining. Reduced sunlight and weaker optical capture could consume that margin; the host engine must determine whether year-10 delivery still meets the target and whether transfer costs actually reduce ore consumption.

proposal.title: Retain the verified seed-only policy
proposal.rationale: Both previous runs met the target with identical mining, so changing orbital radius did not reduce production. Retain zero reinvestment and zero factory expansion to avoid accelerating material consumption and direct all collectors toward delivery. Choose the tested inner orbit and radiator ratio for greater generation per manufactured kilogram. The host already verified this configuration meets the target with substantially less mining than baseline. Further mining reductions are not demonstrated with the allowed controls; the thermal margin is narrow, and excess generation remains curtailed.
